GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS 
RAJYA SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. *256 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28.03.2022 
 
APM for CNG and LNG 
 
*256. SHRI JOSE K. MANI:  
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government has the data regarding the number of LNG stations set up in the country 
in the last two years;   
 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c)whether Government has any plans to come up with an Administered Price Mechanism 
(APM) for both CNG and LNG to ensure firm prices;  
 
(d) if so, the details thereof; 
 
(e) whether Government has any plans to allow a lower rate of GST for entities like State 
Transport Understandings (STUs) through their consumer fuel outlets; and 
 
(f) whether Government is exploring possibilities of direct bulk import of LNG/CNG for the 
consumption of STUs? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS  
(SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI) 
 
 
(a) to (f): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 
*******

STATEMENT REFERRED IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (f) OF THE RAJYA SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. *256 ASKED BY SHRI JOSE K. MANI TO BE ANSWERED 
ON MARCH 28, 2022 REGARDING APM FOR CNG AND LNG 
(a) and (b)  During last two years, 4 LNG stations have been set up across the country by Public 
Sector Undertakings and a Private Entity. GAIL has set up two LNG stations at Cuttack and 
Mandideep and Petronet LNG Limited has set up one LNG station at Kochi. One LNG station in 
the private sector has been set up at Nagpur, Maharashtra. 
(c) to (d) No, Sir. 
(e) Petroleum products namely, petroleum crude, high speed diesel, motor spirit (commonly 
known as petrol), natural gas (which includes CNG and LNG) and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) 
are outside the ambit of GST. 
(f) No, Sir. LNG imports are under open general licensing and any entity can directly import the 
same.

SHRI JOSE K. MANI: Sir, this question is very important in the context of the fact that 
the Leader of the Opposition has requested for a Short Duration Discussion on price 
rise, especially the rise in the prices of petroleum products.  My first supplementary 
question is this. State Transport Undertakings, STUs, are transporting passengers at 
the lowest fares; STUs convert many private vehicle users to use STUs and free the 
road space. When the Government of India promotes conversion from private to 
public transport, why are the State Transport Undertakings charged Rs.22 per litre of 
diesel extra as bulk users?  
 
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Please be brief.  
 
SHRI JOSE K. MANI : Sir, I am putting my question. The same STUs can fill diesel at 
any public petrol bunk without bulk user fee on cash and carry basis.  My question to 
the Minister is: What is the rational for this extra bulk user fee of Rs.22 per litre of 
diesel to STUs like all the State Transport Corporations, especially Kerala State Road 
Transport Corporation?  
 
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN :  Mr. Jose Mani, I would request you that if you take this 
much time, then, others will not get opportunity.  Please be brief in your questions.   
 
SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI : Sir, I want to thank the hon. Member. This question 
relates to LNG and CNG but the question which he has asked in the supplementary 
relates to the price of diesel.  Through you, Sir, let me just inform the House that there 
were two broad processees, State Public Transport providers, to which the hon. 
Member has referred, and some other State Enterprises, which were being supplied 
diesel at wholesale rates. By wholesale rates, I mean, rates which did not factor in 
dealer commission, etc. because they were going to those users directly.  What 
happened, in the aftermath of the pandemic and the military action which is taking 
place in one part of the world, is that global prices went haywire.  In the process, I 
should say, there were wide fluctuations.  As a result, the supplies to wholesalers 
somehow became more expensive than the supplies to the retail points.   So, what 
happened is that a lot of people who were getting discounted diesel started coming 
and queuing up in retail outlets.  I am told that this is a market mechanism functioning 
issue which should resolve itself very soon, as soon as there is stability and one 
knows which way the prices are going.  But the idea for anyone is not to charge the 
wholesalers more than the retailers.

SHRI JOSE K. MANI : Sir, I would make my second supplementary short.  My direct 
question is: Does the Government have any plans to propose STUs to convert any 
stipulated percentage of their existing fleet? Is there any additional subsidy proposed 
to State Transport Undertakings for purchase of new LNG/CNG vehicles?  
 
SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI : Sir, Liquefied National Gas to which the hon. Member 
is referring to is typically a natural gas cooled to a liquid state at about -260 degrees 
Fahrenheit or -162 degrees Celsius.  Sir, LNG is entirely outside the purview of any 
Governmental control. LNG is imported by the private sector directly for use in 
industry.  The Government has encouraged the establishment of what are called LNG 
dispensing stations. There are four of these including one at Kochi in Kerala -- one 
where Liquefied Natural Gas will go straight into heavy duty public transport 
providers.  
Now, out of the four LNG stations, which are dispensing stations that are available in 
the country, two of them are in a position to start dispensing LNG.  We had received 
a letter from the Government of Kerala, of which I have a copy, sometimes in the 
month of August 2021, where they told us that they were proposing to convert 400 
State transport buses into 'use for LNG'.  We have encouraged that.  We have, in 
fact, said that this is a classic case of the chicken and the egg.  The arrangements for 
supply of LNG are there.  Once the vehicles, which can use them, are available, I am 
sure they would start taking the LNG from the dispensing station.   
 
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN:  Please be brief. 
 
SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI: What happens is that the LNG is normally transported 
in cryogenic cylinders.  We are quite happy that another station in Gujarat is actually 
dispensing about 70 kilos in a day. 
 
DR. FAUZIA KHAN:  Sir, according to a recent study, which was made by the Council 
on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW), 70 per cent of Indian households use 
Liquefied Petroleum Gas as their primary cooking fuel but 85 per cent have got 
connections.  So, there is a gap of 15 per cent.  Why is this 15 per cent not using 
that?  The consumer subsidy, which was stopped during the Covid-19 pandemic, 
after rise of Rs.50 in the price, would you reconsider starting of that subsidy?   
 
SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI:  Sir, I want to thank the hon. Member. The reference is 
to the extent to which our population and geographical area are being covered by 
7

CGD. I want to inform the hon. Member that we started this process many, many 
years ago. The 11 th round of bidding is going on currently. After the 11 th and 11- A 
round are complete, we would have over 8 8 per cent of our land area and 98 per cent 
of our population complete so that piped cooking gas can be delivered to 
households. But after the award during the bidding, it typically takes a certain number 
of years.  The only population, which would be left outside, would be those areas in 
the North East and some in Jammu and Kashmir where the physical ability to reach 
the households is a little difficult because they are widely disbursed. Typically, the 
cooking gas, which comes through the pipe, is cheaper and more consumer-friendly 
than that which is distributed through cylinders. 
 The hon. Member asked why the subsidy was stopped.  I would like to inform 
the hon. Member that through the Ujjwala scheme, those who had received the 
Ujjwala benefits earlier, they were given free cylinders during the pandemic. Today, 
we have a situation where the total number of gas connections, which stood at 14 
crores in 2014, has gone up to 30 crores.  This is an ongoing process where through 
the CGD, we would be trying to cover the entire population.  So, this is work in 
progress.   
    
SHRI V. VIJAYASAI REDDY:  Sir, is it true that the Centre is going to set up 1,000 
LNG stations across the country which would attract investment of Rs.10,000 crores?  
If so, how does the Centre propose to identify the locations of these LNG stations?  
Has the Government formulated any policy and time-bound roadmap for setting up 
these LNG stations?   
 
SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI:  Sir, I want to thank the hon. Member. We have a 
roadmap but this is a roadmap which contains only proposal and the idea is to set-up 
one thousand of these along the major highways, etc. It is because, typically, 
Liquefied Natural Gas, by virtue of direct dispensing from the dispensing station, can 
go into heavy duty vehicles which will ply on those, and a certain procedure also for 
setting up is under consideration. I would be happy to share with the hon. Member 
the specifics. We have also disseminated some of this in the Press that we are setting 
up the first 50 LNG fuelling stations, overall one thousand, in the next few years. I will 
be happy to share with him as to what it will take because it will require investment 
both in terms of establishment of the centres and making them functional.

STATEMENT 
 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE RAJYA 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 257 FOR ANSWER ON 28 th MARCH 2022 
REGARDING CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSES UNDER PMAY-U ASKED BY SHRI 
RAJMANI PATEL 
 
(a) Urban Transport, an integral part of urban development, is a State subject. Respective 
State Governments/ Union Territories (UTs) are responsible for initiating and developing urban 
transport infrastructure to various residential areas including Pradhan Mantri AwasYojana – 
Urban (PMAY-U) houses provided by States /UTs.  
 
(b) Government has taken various policy reforms/measures to make the housing market more 
accessible to Economically Weaker Sections of society such as according infrastructure status to 
Affordable Housing thereby  ensuring low cost lending on priority basis, reduction in Goods and 
Service Taxfrom 8% to 1% (without Input Tax Credit), increase in limit of Priority Sector 
Lending for Affordable Housing Projects  from Rs 28 lakh to Rs 35 lakh in metropolitan centres 
(with population of 10 lakh and above) and from  Rs 20 lakh to Rs 25 lakh in other areas and 
setting up of Affordable Housing Fund in National Housing Bank. Further, regulations related to 
Floor Space Index / Floor Area Ratio, change of land use, stamp duty charges / transaction cost 
etc. are being regulated by States /UTs.  The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has issued 
advisories to exempt or make provision for nominal charges towards stamp duty on registration 
of Affordable Housing Projects under PMAY-U. 
 
(c) Government provides interest subsidy upto 2.67 Lakh on home loans under the Credit-
Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS) vertical of the Pradhan Mantri AwasYojana - Urban (PMAY-
U). Under CLSS, there is an interest subsidy of 6.5 % for EWS/ LIG, 4% for Middle Income 
Group-I (MIG-I) and 3% for Middle Income Group-II (MIG-II), calculated on housing loan up to 
₹6 lakh, ₹9 lakh and ₹12 lakh, respectively, over a loan tenure of 20 years.  Credit Linked 
Subsidy Scheme (CLSS) for EWS/LIG is being implemented since 25.06.2015 to 31.03.2022 
while CLSS for MIG was implemented w.e.f.  from 01.01.2017 to 31.03.2021. There is no 
proposal to increase interest subvention.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO, IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF STARRED QUESTION 
NO. *258 TO BE ANSWERED ON 28.03.2022 IN RAJYA SABHA REGARDING “FUNDS 
FOR RENOVATION, EXPANSION AND DESILTATION OF LAKES AND WATER 
BODIES” 
  
(a) & (b)  Water being a State subject, it is for the State Governments to take up water resources 
projects, including works involving desilting, renovation, raising the bunds of lakes and water bodies, 
etc. in their jurisdiction. Role of Government of India is limited to being catalytic, providing technical 
support and in some cases partial financial assistance in terms with the existing schemes under 
implementation.  
  
Government of India is providing financial assistance to the identified schemes under Repair, 
Renovation and Restoration of Water Bodies component of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana 
(PMKSY) - Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP). So far, no project from Karnataka has been included under the 
said scheme during last three years.  
  
However, during 2021-22, Government of Karnataka has submitted proposals for financial assistance 
for repair, renovation and restoration of 1,239 water bodies. The proposals are under appraisal at the 
Regional Office of Central Water Commission (CWC). CWC has sought clarification/ additional 
information from the State Government on some of the proposals, which is awaited. 
 
  
(c) & (d) No special component fund has been provided by Government of India to the  Government 
of Karnataka for the above referred purpose, during last three years.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 259 FOR ANSWER ON 28.03.2022 REGARDING ‘FDI IN 
DEFENCE SECTOR’. 
 
(a) to (c): Yes, Sir. Defence sector is driven by high-end technologies and innovations. The 
sector needs continuous investment for capacity enhancements and creation of state-of-the-art 
technologies and manufacturing facilities to address the requirements of Defence equipment / 
products. In pursuance of the “Make in India” policy, the indigenization of defence products and 
promotion of exports is being provided topmost priority. Large scale efforts are being made by 
the domestic industry to develop such capabilities, however, in areas where such capabilities do 
not exist, FDI by the Global OEMs help to bridge the gap. Besides, FDI also results in creation 
of economic opportunities while saving and bringing precious foreign exchange. Further, this 
gives push to India’s policy of “Make in India & Make for the World”.   
Therefore, to give more thrust and promote FDI in defence sector, Government of India 
liberalized the FDI policy on 17.09.2020 allowing 74% FDI under automatic route and beyond 
74% upto 100% through Government route wherever it is likely to result in access to modern 
technology. While doing so, sufficient safeguards are laid to ensure that security and strategic 
interests of our country are not compromised. During the period from 2001 – 2014, a total FDI 
inflow of about Rs 1382 crore was reported and from 2014 till date, a total FDI of about Rs 3343 
crore has been reported. 
 In addition, the Government has taken many initiatives to strengthen self reliance, import 
substitution and promote R&D in Defence sector, which, inter-alia, include according priority to 
procurement of capital items from domestic sources under Defence Acquisition Procedure 
(DAP)-2020;  Announcement of 18 major defence platforms for industry led design & 
development; Notification of  two ‘Positive Indigenisation Lists’ of total 209 items of Services 
and  one ‘Positive Indigenisation List’ of total 2851 items  of Defence Public Sector 
Undertakings(DPSUs), for which there would be an embargo on the import beyond the timelines 
indicated against them; Simplification of Industrial licensing process with longer validity period; 
Simplification of Make Procedure; Launch of Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) 
scheme involving startups & Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs); Implementation 
of  Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order 2017; Launch of an indigenization 
portal namely SRIJAN to facilitate indigenisation by Indian Industry including MSMEs; 
Reforms in Offset policy with thrust on attracting investment and Transfer of Technology for 
Defence manufacturing by assigning higher multipliers; and Establishment of two Defence 
Industrial Corridors, one each in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. Further, to strengthen the R&D 
base in defence sector, announcement has been made in the Union Budget 2022 – 23 earmarking 
25% of the R&D Budget for industry led R&D.

Statement referred to in reply to Parts (a) to (c) of RAJYA SABHA STARRED 
QUESTION NO. *262 asked by SHRI RAM SHAKAL regarding ‘JIYO PARSI 
SCHEME’. 
 
(a) to (c): Yes, Sir. The Ministry of Minority Affairs implements a community-specific 
scheme namely ‘Jiyo Parsi’- Scheme for containing population decline of Parsis of 
India. The Scheme has three components: (i) Advocacy- includes counseling of 
couples with fertility issues, marriage, family and elderly counseling including 
workshops on relationship management, parenting, drug awareness etc. (ii) Health 
of Community- to provide financial assistance to Parsi parents to meet the expenses 
towards creche/child care, assistance to elderly etc. (iii) Medical Assistance- includes 
financial assistance for Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) which also 
includes In-vitro Fertilization and Intra Cytoplasmic Injection (ICS) and other modes.  
 
The scheme is being implemented by a Project Implementing Agency (PIA) namely, 
Parzor Foundation. So far, 359 babies have been born with the assistance under this 
Scheme.  
 
The details of the Jiyo Parsi Scheme may be seen at Ministry’s website-`  
https://www.minorityaffairs.gov.in
.  
 
During the years 2018-19 to 2021-22, Rs. 16.86 crore have been released to the 
implementing agency for implementation of this Scheme.

STATEMENT 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY OF PARTS (a) TO (e) OF THE RAJYA SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 264 (9 th POSITION) FOR ANSWER ON 28.03.2022 
REGARDING SCM PROJECTS IN TAMIL NADU. 
 
(a) to (e): Government of India launched the Smart Cities Mission (SCM) on 25 June 2015. 100 
Smart Cities have been selected through 4 rounds of competition from January 2016 to June 2018. 11 
cities of Tamil Nadu, i.e., Chennai, Coimbatore, Erode, Madurai, Salem, Thanjavur, Thoothukudi, 
Tiruchirappalli, Tirunelveli, Tiruppur and Vellore have been selected for development as Smart Cities.  
 
As per SCM Guidelines, Central Government will provide financial support to the extent of         ₹ 
48,000 crore over five years i.e., on an average ₹ 100 crore per city per year.  An equal amount on a 
matching basis will be contributed by the State Government/Urban Local Body (ULB).  As on 4 
March 2022, Government of India has released   ₹ 29,213.60 crore for 100 Smart Cities, out of which 
₹ 25,177.65 crore (86%) has been utilized.  These Cities have tendered out 6,928 projects worth ₹ 
1,91,238 crore; work orders have been issued in 6,282 projects worth ₹ 1,65,503 crore; 3,576 projects 
worth ₹ 59,958 crore have been completed.   
 
The details of selection, status of projects, funds released and utilized by Smart Cities in Tamil Nadu 
is given in Annexure-I. 
 
The progress of implementation in cities selected under SCM depends on their round of selection. The 
process of competitive selection of cities spanned from January 2016 to June 2018. After selection, 
the time taken for setting up the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV), formation of the Board of Directors, 
hiring of human resources, preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) and tendering has been 
observed to take 12 to 18 months in different Cities. In addition, COVID-19 pandemic related 
lockdowns and other unprecedented situations led to temporary interruptions in execution of Smart 
City works across the country. However, Smart Cities commenced works after un-lockdown in right 
earnest. Keeping in mind that each city needs to get at least 5 years to execute their projects and that 
the 100 th city, Shillong, was selected in June 2018, the period of implementation of SCM has been 
extended upto June 2023. All Smart Cities are expected to complete their projects within the 
stipulated time. 
 
The implementation of SCM at the city level is done by the SPV created for the purpose. These SPVs 
are registered under the Companies Act, 2013 and are jointly owned in 50:50 ratio by respective State 
Government/Union Territory (UT) & Urban Local Body (ULB). These SPVs are responsible for 
appraisal, approval, implementation, management, monitoring and evaluation of projects which are 
part of their Smart City Plans. Any complaints/grievances as and when received by the Government of 
India with regard to implementation of Smart City projects, are forwarded to the respective State 
Government/UT/Smart City for taking appropriate remedial measures.

JOB LOSSES DURING PANDEMIC 
265. SHRI RIPUN BORA
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether Government is aware of job losses during the last three
years in the private sector companies in carrier service, in 
operation and maintenance of airports; 
(b) whether Government has taken any measures to assist the
people who have lost their jobs during the pandemic and also as a 
result of private sector takeover of airports; 
(c) if so, the details thereof and, if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the reasons for not having discussion and/or talk with the carrier
organizations to restore the employment to pre COVID-19 level? 
ANSWER 
 (Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia)Minister of CIVIL AVIATION  
(a) to (d) A statement is laid on the table of the Rajya Sabha.
****** 
Statement in reply to Rajya Sabha Starred Question No 265 for 28th 
March 2022 
(a) to (d) According to industry sources, the details of job losses are
as under: 
(i) Total number of airline employees in India has declined from
around 74,800 as on 31st March 2020 to around 65,600 as on 31st 
December 2021. 
60

(ii) Total number of employees in airport sector has declined from 
around 73,400 as on 31st March 2020 to around 65,700 as on 31st 
December 2021. 
 
(iii) Total number of employees in ground handling sector has 
declined from around 30,800 as on 31st March 2020 to around 
27,600 as on 31st December 2021. 
(iv) Total number of employees in air cargo sector has increased 
from around 9,600 as on 31st March 2020 to around 10,500 as on 
31st December 2021. 
 
 
 
The total job loss in airlines, airports, ground handling and air cargo 
sector is around 19,200.  The job loss is around 10% of the total jobs 
(around 1.9 lakh) in these sectors. The Government has held 
discussions with industry participants and stakeholders to address 
the challenges facing the industry. 
 
 
Air traffic during 2 020-21 witnessed a massive fall of 66% over the 
previous year due to the Covid pandemic. During the last two years, 
the COVID-19 pandemic has adversely impacted the revenue 
streams of businesses including aviation sector. Under normal 
circumstances, airfares are neither established nor regulated by the 
Government. However, due to the unprecedented circumstances, 
fare bands with upper and lower limits were introduced by the 
Government as a special measure. The fare bands serve the dual 
purpose of protecting the interests of the travelers as well as of the 
airlines. 
 
Consequent to spread of COVID-19 pandemic, airline operations 
were suspended in March, 2020 in the country. Based on the 
improvement in COVID situation, a calibrated resumption of 
domestic operations was allowed in May 2020 with various 
protocols for safe air travel. After assessing the situation and 
passenger demand for air travel, from time to time the capacity 
restrictions on 
61

domestic operations have been lifted with effect from 18th October 
2021. 
 
 
With the massive nationwide Covid-vaccination drive undertaken by 
the Government, revival in air traffic in 2021-22, opening of 
international flight from 27th March 2022, establishment of new 
airports, expansion of existing airports and airlines etc, growth of  
the Indian aviation sector is likely to result in increase of jobs 
opportunities in the sector.

the land to a condition which is fit for growth of fodder, flora, fauna etc.

& Works related to Border Areas (RMBA) was approved by Government of India. The FMBAP scheme was 
further extended for the year 2020-21. However, FMBAP scheme was approved for prioritised completion of 
the spillover works in respect of 83 ongoing projects as well as for outstanding payments of the completed 
works which were included earlier under FMP during Xl & Xll Plans. The scheme had a provision only for 
clearing the committed liabilities of ongoing and completed projects as per extant Xl / Xll Plan guidelines and

central funding. Only those projects which are techno economically accepted by Advisory Committee of 
Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation (DoWR, RD & GR) and, 
thereafter, cleared by Investment Clearance Committee of DoWR, RD&GR are considered for central funding 
under FMBAP.

th March, 2022 for central

BAN ON IMPORT OF DRONES 
2722.    DR. L. HANUMANTHAIAH                    
             SHRI RAJMANI PATEL                       
             SMT PHULO DEVI NETAM                    
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the notification of February 9, 2022 banning the import 
of drones will have any direct effect on the use of imported drones 
within the country in commercial and leisure use; 
(b) if so, the details thereof with special regards to permissions and 
regulations that have been altered; 
(c) whether Government believes that the current notification will 
have any effect on the size of the grey markets for drones; 
(d) whether Government has taken any steps to curb illegal drones 
from unregulated trade routes; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof and, if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      
(GEN. (DR) V. K. SINGH (RETD)) 
(a) to (e) Yes sir.  The ban on import of drones will have an effect on 
the use of imported drones within the country in commercial and 
leisure use.   
 
 
As per Rule 14 of the Drone Rules, 2021 notified on 25th August 
2021, any person owning a drone imported into India before 30th 
November, 2021 was allowed to obtain a Unique Identification 
Number (UIN) for the same through the Government's online 
DigitalSky Platform.  Thus, a prior notice period of more than 90 
days was provided to drone importers.  
81

 
 
 
According to Rule 14 of the Drone Rules, 2021, no person shall 
operate an unmanned aircraft system without first registering it on 
the digital sky platform and obtaining a unique identification 
number, unless exempted.  Importing and operating an illegal drone 
may invite penal action as per law.   
 
 
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) vide notification 
No. 54/2015-2020 dated 9th February 2022 prohibited import of 
drones in completely built up (CBU), semi knocked down (SKD) or 
completely knocked down (CKD) form, except for R&D, defence and 
security purposes. 
 
 
DGFT has informed officers and staff of Central Board of Indirect 
Taxes and Customs about the ban on import of drones and the same 
has been implemented across the country with effect from 9th 
February 2022.

Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:-
 
the steps taken for early delivery of services at regional airports of Jharkhand,
especially Deoghar and Bokaro airports, which is a very important project, started
by Government?
 
ANSWER
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
 
 (GEN. (DR) V. K. SINGH (RETD))
 
 
Ministry of Civil Aviation launched Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) -
UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) on 21-10-2016 to stimulate regional air
connectivity and making air travel affordable to the masses. The primary objective
of RCS is to facilitate / stimulate regional air connectivity by connecting
unserved/underserved airports/heliports/water aerodromes. UDAN is a market
driven scheme. Interested airlines based on their assessment of demand on
particular routes submit their proposals at the time of bidding under UDAN.
An airport which is included in the awarded routes of UDAN and requires
upgradation / development for commencement of RCS operations, is developed
under "Revival/upgradation of unserved and underserved airports/heliports/water
aerodromes" Scheme. The Government of India has approved a budget of Rs. 4500
crore for revival of existing unserved / underserved airports / airstrips of the State
Governments, Airports Authority of India, Public Sector Undertakings and Civil
Enclaves.
Airports Authority of India (AAI), the Implementing Agency, has identified
Bokaro for operationalization of RCS flights under UDAN Scheme. Further, on the
request of the State Government of Jharkhand, UDAN bids for operation of RCS
flights from Deoghar to Kolkata, Ranchi and Patna, are received. However,
consent of the State Government is required for 100 % Viability Gap Funding
(VGF) for these State  sponsored RCS routes, before award. Deoghar airport
belongs to AAI in Joint Venture with State Government and has a single runway
09/27 having dimension 2500m x 45m. The State Government has to construct the
approach road from highway to Airport, provide security services and remove
2739. SHRI DEEPAK PRAKASH

and international flights, during last two years;
(b) whether any credit guarantee is provided to the air operators through
Government, if so, details thereof?
(c) whether the flights both domestic and international as scheduled prior to March,
2020 would be allowed to be operated from end of March, 2022;
(d) if so, details thereof;
(e) whether airfares would be reduced in case of more competition, if so, the details
thereof; and
(f) whether COVID-19 protocol would be followed in the flight operations and for
passengers, with details thereof?
 
ANSWER
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
 
 (GEN. (DR) V. K. SINGH (RETD))
 
 
(a) & (b): The aviation sector in India has been affected adversely due to severe
disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. The estimated loss incurred by
Airlines and Airports in India in the financial year 2020-21 is approximately Rs.
19,564 crore and Rs. 5,116 crore respectively. The Government has extended the
Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme to the Airlines. The scheme provides
for 100% guarantee to member lending institutions in respect of eligible credit
facility extended by them to their borrowers in the Civil Aviation (scheduled and
non-scheduled airlines, chartered flight operators, air ambulances, airports and
ground handling units) sectors subject to the conditions mentioned therein.
 
(c) to (f): Ministry of Civil Aviation vide Order No. 27/2021 dated 12.10.2021 has
restored the scheduled domestic air operations w.e.f. 18th October, 2021 without
any capacity restriction. With regard to scheduled international operation, to/from
country, DGCA (Directorate General of Civil Aviation) has issued Circular dated
08.03.2022 for resumption of scheduled commercial international passenger

services to/from India w.e.f. 27.03.2022 i.e. start of Summer schedule, 2022.
 
Ministry vide order dated 12.10.2021 has restored the scheduled domestic Air
operations w.e.f. 18.10.2021 without any capacity restriction wherein the
Airline/Airport operators has been advised to ensure that the Guidelines to contain
the spread of Covid are strictly adhered to and Covid appropriate behaviour is
strictly enforced by them during travel.
 
The airfares are not regulated by the Government. Under the provisions of Sub
Rule(1) of Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules, 1937, every air transport undertaking
engaged in scheduled air services is required to establish tariff having regard to all
relevant factors, including cost of operation, characteristics of services, reasonable
profit and the generally prevailing tariff. Airlines are free to charge reasonable air
fares as per their operational viabilities subject to compliance of above said order.
The airlines are compliant to the Sub Rule (2) of Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules,
1937 as long as fares charged by them is in line with fares displayed on their
website.

Zero output growth 
  
2750. SHRI P. BHATTACHARYA:

(a) whether coal sector reported zero output growth in the current year;  
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and  
(c) the steps taken to correct the situation in future? 
 
Answer 
  
MINISTER OF  PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS, COAL AND MINES 
(SHRI PRALHAD JOSHI) 
  
(a)&(b): No Sir . All India coal production during April- February 2021- 22 was 
681.52 MT registering a growth of 9.9%.  
(c): In order to increase more coal production, the focus of the Government is 
on accelerating domestic production of coal through allocation of more coal 
blocks, pursuing with State Government for assistance in land acquisition and 
coordinated efforts with Railways for movement of coal. 
  
In addition, the following steps have been taken by Government to further 
enhance the production of the coal in the country.   
1. Commercial Auction of coal on revenue share mechanism: Since 
Launch of auction of coal mines for commercial mining in June 2020, a total of 
4 rounds of auction have been conducted in which total 292 coal mines were 
offered.  In 3 rounds, 42 coal mines have been successfully auctioned. Further, 
in respect of 4 th round of auction, bids were opened on 02.03.2022 and 2 or 
more bids have been received in respect of 5 coal mines and 6 coal mines have 
fetched single bids. 
2. Allowed sale of excess coal production : The Ministry of Coal has 
amended Mineral Concession Rules, 1960 with a view to allowing sale of coal or 
lignite, on payment of additional amount to the State Government, by the 
lessee of a captive mine up to 50 percent of the total coal or lignite produced in 
a financial year, after meeting the requirement of the end use plant linked with 
the mine. Earlier this year, the Mines and Minerals (Development & Regulation) 
Act had been amended to this effect. This is applicable for both the private and 
public sector captive mines. With this amendment, the Government has paved 
the way for releasing of additional coal in the market by greater utilization of 
mining capacities of captive coal and lignite blocks, which were being only 
partly utilized owing to limited production of coal for meeting only their captive 
needs.

(SHRI PRALHAD JOSHI)  
  
(a): Detailed physical status of Stabilization work in Deulbera & Handidhua Collieries of 
Talcher Coalfield of MCL is as under:- 
(i)  In Handidhua Colliery, total 5,85,000 m 3 of sand was assessed as requirement of sand 
stowing to stabilize the underground workings in identified areas. Hydraulic sand stowing

underground workings of Deulbera and Handidhua Collieries by sand stowing by Hydro 
Pneumatic sand stowing method. Since, the surface land is not vested with MCL and it belongs 
to private/Govt. land unauthorizedly occupied, there are obstruction from the tenants/locals in 
renting their land for drilling / sand stowing / sand transportation to site. For this, necessary 
intervention and support are being taken from the State administration and local authorities.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2757 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28.03.2022 
  
POLLUTION DUE TO COAL MINING 
  
2757 Dr. Fauzia Khan:  
  
Will the Minister of Coal be pleased to state :- 
  
(a) whether the coal mines in the country produce and emit a large quantity of Suspended 
Particulate Matter (SPM) in the atmosphere and pollute the area around to a large extent; 
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government to combat this pollution from the coal mines; 
(c) whether Government has plans to control pollution and protect the environment; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF COAL, MINES AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
(SHRI PRALHAD JOSHI) 
  
(a) & (b) :  Coal mining, like any other developmental activity, does have impacts on native 
environment, which are generally contained within the mining area itself.  One of the impacts of 
mining activities involving drilling, blasting, loading and transport of coal is generation and 
dispersion of suspended particulate matter in the atmosphere for which various air pollution 
control measures including those prescribed in the EMP/EC/CTO are taken by mine operators to 
minimize the impact and maintain 
 air quality standards as prescribed in MoEFCC Notification 
No. G.S.R. 742(E) dated 25.09.2000 for coal mines :- 
  
 Generation and propagation of dust is controlled at source by installation of fixed 
sprinklers at CHPs, coal stock yards, weighbridges and along transportation roads. In 
major CHPs, fixed sprinklers have been provided at the transfer points and bunkers 
 Mobile water sprinkler are deployed along the haul roads and road transport road 
 Long throw fog canons have been deployed in mines and industrial establishments Th e 
mist type water spraying system have been installed along the conveyor belts / Bunkers in 
major coal handling plants. The sides of CHPs are covered by side cladding with GI 
Sheet to control pollution at source. 
 Control blasting techniques with proper delay detonators and explosives are used for 
mitigation of dust generation and ground vibration during blasting operations. 
 Coal companies are deploying modern equipment having environment friendly features, 
like Surface Miner in coal that eliminates the drilling, blasting and crushing operations in 
coal and hence, in turn, obviates pollution caused due to these operations. 
154

 Use of drills fitted with wet drilling and dust extractors in order to control generation of 
dust. 
 To avoid spillage of Coal from trucks on road - all loaded coal transporting trucks are 
covered by tarpaulin and also overloading of trucks are prohibited 
 Transport haul roads are kept well maintained and Concrete/black topped roads are being 
developed for better stability and durability; 
 Mines 
have deployed mechanical sweepers and other methods for dry sweeping of roads. 
 First Mile Connectivity (FMC) projects are being implemented to replace road transport 
through mechanical loading and conveying systems 
 Avenue and peripheral plantation to arrest the propagation and dispersion of dust 
significantly. 
 Installation of Wind barriers for dust trapping. 
 Plantation on inactive OB Dumps to minimize soil erosion; 
 
 
(c), (d) & (e) : The existing statutory environmental framework provides adequate safeguards to 
minimize the adverse environmental impacts of mining on native environment. 
  
Before commencement of mining, it is mandatory for all mines to obtain Environmental 
Clearance (EC) from MoEF&CC for which, a detailed Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) i s 
carried out and accordingly a comprehensive Environment management Plan (EMP) with all 
safeguards is prepared. The EIA/EMP is deliberated in detail by the Environmental Appraisal 
Committee (EAC) of MoEF&CC before issuance of EC for the mine. In addition, all mining 
projects have to obtain Consent to Establish (CTE) and Consent to Operate (CTO) from State 
Pollution Control Boards (SPCB). These Environmental Permits stipulate all necessary 
conditions including mitigation measures to protect the environment. 
 
 
The stipulated conditions of EC/CTO/CTE/FC and the mitigative measures proposed in 
EMP are necessarily complied to maintain the appropriate environmental standards in mining 
regions. 
 Comprehensive environmental monitoring mechanism, for assessing the efficacy of 
mitigation measures, is undertaken as prescribed in the Environment (Protection) Act & Rules 
and EC conditions. All the pollutants are kept within the prescribed limit and the compliance 
report is submitted to regulatory agencies on routine basis. 
 
 
All mitigation measures are taken up by coal companies, for which funds are earmarked 
in project reports/schemes/mine closure plans/revenue and capital budgets of respective projects. 
  
Thus, the present system of regulating the environment matters through MoEF&CC and 
CPCB/ SPCBs has inbuilt mechanism in place for environmental protection in and around coal 
mining areas.

during the current year;

sector;  
(c) if so, the details thereof and, if not, the reasons therefor; and  
(d) the steps taken/proposed to be taken by Government to improve the coal 
production in the country?   
Answer 
MINISTER OF  PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS, COAL AND MINES 
(SHRI PRALHAD JOSHI) 
  
(a):  During the current year 2021- 22, the coal production target of Coal India 
Limited (CIL) has been fixed at 670 Million Tonnes (MT).  
(b)&(c): In 2021- 22 (upto 10 th March, 2022), Coal India Limited (CIL) has 
dispatched 506.29 MT, with a 23% growth over last year. Similarly, SCCL and 
captive coal blocks have dispatched 50.38 MT and 77.5 MT coal to power sector 
(upto 10th March 2022) which is 34.2% and 40% more than the same period of 
last year. 
Coal supplies to power sector is being regularly monitored by an Inter-
Ministerial Sub Group comprising of representatives from Ministries of Power, 
Ministry of Coal, Ministry of Railways, Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Coal 
India Limited (CIL), Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) and NTPC 
etc. to take various operational decisions to enhance supply of coal to thermal 
power plants as well as for meeting any contingent situations relating to Power 
Sector including to alleviate critical coal stock position in power plants. 
(d): In order to increase coal production, the focus of the Government is on 
accelerating domestic production of coal through allocation of more coal 
blocks, pursuing with State Government for assistance in land acquisition and 
coordinated efforts with Railways for movement of coal.  
  
In addition, t he following action has been taken by Government to further 
enhance the production of the coal in the country.  
 
  
1. Commercial Auction of coal on revenue share mechanism: Since 
Launch of auction of coal mines for commercial mining in June 2020, a 
total of 4 rounds of auction have been conducted in which total 292 coal 
mines were offered.  In 3 rounds, 42 coal mines have been successfully

on 02.03.2022 and 2 or more bids have been received in respect of 5 coal 
mines and 6 coal mines have fetched single bids. 
2. Allowed sale of excess coal production : The Ministry of Coal has 
amended Mineral Concession Rules, 1960 with a view to allowing sale of 
coal or lignite, on payment of additional amount to the State 
Government, by the lessee of a captive mine up to 50 percent of the total 
coal or lignite produced in a financial year, after meeting the requirement 
of the end use plant linked with the mine. Earlier this year, the Mines 
and Minerals (Development & Regulation) Act had been amended to this 
effect. This is applicable for both the private and public sector captive 
mines. With this amendment, the Government has paved the way for 
releasing of additional coal in the market by greater utilization of mining 
capacities of captive coal and lignite blocks, which were being only partly 
utilized owing to limited production of coal for meeting only their captive 
needs.
 
3. Rolling auction: In order to expedite the process for conducting auction 
and to carry out more rounds of auction in a year, a mechanism of 
rolling auctions of coal mines has been planned. Under this mechanism, 
upon completion of the electronic auction process of a tranche, the next 
tranche of auction would be launched for following mines: 
i. Mines where no bid or only single bid was received in the previous 
tranche of auction (except for those mines where Ministry of Coal decides 
to go for second attempt of auction) 
ii. New mines, if any, identified by Ministry of Coal

mine in India. Now, the complete process shall be facilitated through 
Single Window Clearance Portal, which will map not only the relevant 
application formats, but also process flow for grant of approvals or 
clearances.
   
5. Coal India Limited (CIL) has envisaged a coal production programme of

(a) whether Government is aware of the coal shortage faced by thermal power plants of 
Karnataka, if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(b) whether due to the coal shortage, the State has witnessed the disruption of power 
supply, if so, the action plan initiated to avoid the reoccurrence of the problem? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS, COAL AND MINES  
(SHRI PRALHAD JOSHI) 
(a): Due to increased demand of power, less power generation by imported coal based 
power plants and some interruption in supply of coal due to heavy rains, the coal stock 
at the power plants end depleted to 7.2 Million Tonne (MT) as on 8 th October, 
2021.  Subsequently with increased coal supplies, the coal stock has started increasing 
and has now reached 25.58 MT as on 21.03.2022. In 2021-22 (upto Feb'22), the total 
domestic coal supplied to the power plant was 611.43 Million Tonnes (MT) (provisional) 
which is more than 124.45 MT against the supply of  486.98 during same period of the 
previous year. 
In 2021-22 (upto 15.3.2022), SCCL supplied 7.8 MT coal against the prorata linkages of 
9.0 MT to the thermal power plants of Karnataka under FSA, despite huge outstanding 
dues of Rs.573.80 Crore as on 28.02.2022. Similarly, CIL supplied 2.946 MT coal 
against the prorata Annual Contracted Quantity (ACQ) of 3.92 MT to the thermal power 
plants of Karnataka under FSA in 2021-22, despite  outstanding dues of Rs.121.33 
Crore as on 28.02.2022.  Less supply of coal can be attributed to the fact that KPCL 
had regulated coal supply by not placing adequate programmes.  
KPCL was  offered additional coal of 2.74 Lakh Tonnes (LT) (Round-1) and 2.50 LT 
(Round 2) by CIL through RCR mode.  KPCL  lifted only 1.24 LT during Round-1.   
In addition, the following captive coal blocks, namely Baranj I to IV, Manora Deep and 
Kiloni, has been allocated to KPCL for their end use plants.  In 2021-22, the scheduled 
production of these coal blocks is 2.5 MT, against which  1.043 MT has been 
produced.  Besides, Durgapur-II/Taraimar & Durgapur-II/Saria and Mandikini coal 
blocks have also been allocated to KPCL.

(b): Central Electricity Authority has informed that the state power utility has intimated 
that against the energy requirement of about 64.39 Billion Units (BU) during the period 
April, 2021 to February, 2022 in the state of Karnataka, about 64.38 BU was supplied. 
Thus, the overall power supply position has been comfortable in the state of Karnataka 
during the current year 2021-22 (April, 2021 to February, 2022) with energy supplied 
being almost commensurate to the energy requirement.

Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether only 47.6 per cent of the total number of houses sanctioned for urban areas under 
various urban development schemes have been constructed so far; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the details thereof;   
(c) whether Government is pushing for more private participation in Affordable Rental Housing 
Complex (ARHC);

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE

(a) & (b): Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) is supplementing the efforts of 
States/Union Territories (UTs) through Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U) since 
2015 to provide all weather pucca houses with all basic amenities for all eligible families/ 
beneficiaries. Eligible beneficiaries can avail the benefit of PMAY-U through any of the four 
verticals i.e., Beneficiary led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), In-
Situ Slum Redevelopment (ISSR) and Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS).Based on the 
project proposals submitted by States/UTs, more than 115 lakh houses have been sanctioned 
across the country, out of which more than 95 lakh have been grounded and more than 56 lakh 
have been completed/ delivered to the beneficiaries so far. Completion of projects generally 
takes 12-18 months under BLC vertical and 24-36 months under AHP vertical of the Scheme. 
Therefore, there is always a lag between sanctioning, construction, and completion of houses. 
States/UTs have been advised to ground and complete all remaining sanctioned houses within 
the stipulated timeline as per Detailed Project Reports.   
(c) & (d): Yes, Sir. The Affordable Rental Housing Complexes (ARHCs)as a sub-scheme of 
PMAY-U is being implemented through two models as under: 
i. Model-1: Utilizing existing Government funded vacant houses to convert into ARHCs 
through Public Private Partnership (PPP) or by Public Agencies 
ii. Model-2: Construction, Operation & Maintenance of ARHCs by Public/ Private Entities on 
their own available vacant land.

Under Model-2 of the Scheme, all land owning Public/Private Entities are encouraged to 
construct ARHCs for urban migrants/ poor who are engaged in their own industries as well as for 
nearby establishments. MoHUA has issued the Expression of Interest (EoI) three times to 
shortlist the Public/ Private Entities for construction of ARHCs for urban migrants/ poor on their 
own available vacant land. Pursuant to said EoI, proposals for construction of 78,885 new ARHC 
units have been sanctioned. In order to provide impetus to the Private participation under this 
Scheme, following incentives/ benefits have been provisioned as mentioned below: 
i. Exemption of Income Tax on any profits and gains derived from operation of ARHCs. 
ii. Exemption of GST on any profits and gains derived from operation of ARHCs at par with 
rental services of residential premises. 
iii. Project finance/loan at lower interest rate through concessional window under Affordable 
Housing Fund (AHF) by Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) and Priority Sector Lending 
(PSL) by Commercials Banks. 
iv. Provision of “Use Permission” changes for houses on vacant land, if needed. 
v. 50% additional Floor Area Ratio (FAR)/ Floor Space Index (FSI), free of cost.  
vi. Single window approval of design/ drawings and other statutory approvals within 30 days. 
vii. Necessary trunk infrastructure facilities up to the project site without any additional cost to 
the Entity. 
viii. Municipal services such as water supply, electricity, house/ property tax, sewerage/ septage 
charge etc. for operation of ARHCs levied at par with residential projects. 
ix. Additional grant in the form of Technological Innovation Grant (TIG) by MoHUA for 
using innovative, sustainable, green and disaster-resilient technologies as well as building 
materials for cost effective, faster and quality construction of ARHCs.

(a) to (d):  National Urban Digital Mission (NUDM) was launched in February 2021 to facilitate 
electronic delivery of municipal services to citizens across towns and cities of the country. NUDM aims 
to build shared digital infrastructure which will include elements like foundational digital building 
blocks, ready-to-use platforms, standards, specifications, and frameworks for improving urban 
governance. It supports States and Union Territories (UTs) in delivering online municipal services to all 
their citizens including women and transgenders. The implementation of NUDM is being anchored by 
the Centre for Digital Governance (CDG) at National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA). Stakeholders’ 
consultation is part of the approach towards implementation of NUDM, and engagements have been held 
with various State Governments and relevant stakeholders through various online and offline channels.  
Presently, there are no public private partnership projects undertaken under NUDM in the State of West 
Bengal. There is no State/UT-wise budgetary allocation under NUDM, including the State of West 
Bengal.

Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of central and state assistance sanctioned so far for 100 smart cities 
  selected under the Smart Cities Mission (SCM), city-wise and year-wise; 
(b)  the details of central assistance released so far, city-wise, and year-wise; and

  wise and year-wise?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI KAUSHAL KISHORE) 
 
(a) to (c): Government of India launched the Smart Cities Mission (SCM) on 25 June 2015. 100 Smart 
cities have been selected through 4 rounds of competition from January 2016 to June 2018.  
 
As per SCM Guidelines, Central Government will provide financial support to the extent of ₹ 48,000 
crore over five years i.e., on an average ₹ 100 crore per city per year.  An equal amount on a matching 
basis will be contributed by the State Government/Urban Local Body (ULB).

which ₹ 25,177.65 crore (86%) has been utilized. The State/City-wise details of funds released by 
Central Government & utilization thereof by Smart Cities is given in Annexure-I. 
 
As on 4 March 2022, 100 Smart Cities have tendered out 6,928 projects worth ₹ 1,91,238 crore; work

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2792 
TO BE ANSWERED ON MARCH 28, 2022 
 
IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SMART CITIES MISSION 
NO. 2792.   SHRI MAHESH PODDAR : 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
(a)  the number of projects pending under the Smart Cities Mission and the details thereof, 
  State-wise; 
(b)  the amount of Central assistance allocated for the project in the last three years and 
  how much has been utilized till date, the details thereof; and 
(c)   the number of people rehabilitated after eviction for the implementation of the scheme 
  and funds allocated for that and the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI KAUSHAL KISHORE) 
 
(a):   Government of India launched the Smart Cities Mission (SCM) on 25 June 2015. 100 Smart 
cities have been selected through 4 rounds of competition from January 2016 to June 2018. As on 4 
March 2022, 100 Smart Cities have tendered out 6,928 projects worth ₹ 1,91,238 crore; work orders 
have been issued in 6,282 projects worth ₹ 1,65,503 crore; 3,576 projects worth ₹ 59,958 crore have 
been completed.  The State/City-wise status of Smart City projects is given in Annexure-I. 
 
(b):  As per SCM Guidelines, Central Government will provide financial support to the extent of ₹ 
48,000 crore over five years i.e., on an average ₹ 100 crore per city per year.  An equal amount on a 
matching basis will be contributed by the State Government/Urban Local Body (ULB).  As on 4 March 
2022, Government of India has released   ₹ 29,213.60 crore for 100 Smart Cities, out of which ₹ 
25,177.65 crore (86%) has been utilized. The State/City-wise details of funds released by Central 
Government & utilization thereof by Smart Cities is given in Annexure-II. 
 
(c):  Since Land and Colonization are State subjects, State Governments issue policies/guidelines for 
re-development/rehabilitation etc.  Under SCM, projects including those related to re-
development/rehabilitation are proposed and implemented by cities in accordance with their Smart City 
Plans (SCPs). No specific guidelines have been issued under SCM for the purpose and no separate funds 
are allocated under SCM for the same.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2793 
TO BE ANSWEREDON MARCH 28, 2022 
 
REHABILITATION OF SLUM DWELLERS 
 
NO. 2793.   SHRI RIPUN BORA:  
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government had proposed housing for all in 2015, targeting the rehabilitation of slum 
dwellers; 
(b) if so, the details of slums in top cities reported from 2015 to 2020 and promotion of affordable 
housing for weaker section during this period; and  
(c) by when Government will provide sustainable housing to all slum dwellers through its 
rehabilitation programme and the timeline thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI KAUSHAL KISHORE) 
 
 
(a) to (c): Land and Colonization are State subjects. Therefore, schemes related to housing for 
Economically Weaker Section (EWS) including slum dwellers are being implemented by State/ 
Union Territories (UTs). However, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs is supplementing the 
efforts of State/ UTs by providing Central Assistance under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 
(PMAY-U) since 25.06.2015 for construction of houses for all eligible families/ beneficiaries. 
Eligible beneficiaries including slum dwellers can avail the benefit of PMAY-U through any of the 
four verticals i.e. Beneficiary-led Construction, Affordable House in Partnership, In-Situ Slum 
Redevelopment and Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme. 
PMAY-U mission is being implemented with an aim to provide all weather pucca house with all 
basic amenities to all eligible beneficiaries/ families including slum dwellers across the country. 
Based on the project proposals submitted by States/UTs, so far more than 115 lakh houses have 
been sanctionedin all urban areas including top twenty cities, out of which more than 95 lakhhave 
been grounded andmore than 56 lakh have been completed/ delivered to the beneficiaries.  
The details of affordable houses sanctioned for EWS including slum dwellers during 2015-2020 
under PMAY-U in top twenty cities are at Annexure.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2794 
TO BE ANSWERED ON MARCH 28, 2022 
SPV FORMED BY CITIES 
NO. 2794.    SHRI JAWHAR SIRCAR : 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of smart cities which are part of the Smart Cities Mission at present and 
   whether all of them have created their Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) and raised their own 
    funds; 
 
(b)  the amount which the Centre and State Governments have provided to each and other 
   funds available with them; 
 
(c)  the details of funding and progress under each city; and 
 
(d) specific progress achieved by the Smart Cities Mission so far and the problems that 
  plague it? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI KAUSHAL KISHORE) 
 
(a) to (d):  Government of India launched the Smart Cities Mission (SCM) on 25 June 2015. 100 
Smart cities have been selected through 4 rounds of competition from January 2016 to June 2018. The 
implementation of SCM at the city level is done by a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) created for the 
purpose. All the 100 Smart Cities have established their SPVs.   
As per SCM Guidelines, Central Government will provide financial support to the extent of        ₹ 48,000 
crore over five years i.e., on an average ₹ 100 crore per city per year.  An equal amount on a matching 
basis will be contributed by the State Government/Urban Local Body (ULB).  As on 4 March 2022, 
Government of India has released   ₹ 29,213.60 crore for 100 Smart Cities, out of which ₹ 25,177.65 
crore (86%) has been utilized. The State/City-wise details of funds released by Central Government & 
utilization thereof by Smart Cities is given in Annexure-I. 
 
As on 4 March 2022, 100 Smart Cities have tendered out 6,928 projects worth ₹ 1,91,238 crore; work 
orders have been issued in 6,282 projects worth ₹ 1,65,503 crore; 3,576 projects worth        ₹ 59,958 
crore have been completed.  The State/City-wise status of Smart City projects is given in Annexure-II. 
 
The period of implementation of SCM has been extended upto June 2023 and all Smart Cities are 
expected to complete their projects within the stipulated time.

SCM IN GUJARAT 
NO. 2795.          SHRI NARANBHAI J. RATHWA: 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
(a)  the names of smart cities which have been selected in the State of Gujarat under Smart 
Cities Mission (SCM); 
 
(b)  the total funds allotted and utilized so far on these cities and the progress of various 
   development projects in these cities in Gujarat; and 
 
(c) whether the project of Smart Cities Mission is likely to be scrapped and, if so, the 
   details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI KAUSHAL KISHORE) 
 
(a):  Government of India launched the Smart Cities Mission (SCM) on 25 June 2015. 100 Smart 
cities have been selected through 4 rounds of competition from January 2016 to June 2018. In the State 
of Gujarat, 6 cities namely Ahmedabad, Dahod, Gandhinagar, Rajkot, Surat & Vadodara have been 
selected for development as Smart Cities. 
 
(b):  As per SCM Guidelines, Central Government will provide financial support to the extent of ₹ 
48,000 crore over five years i.e., on an average ₹ 100 crore per city per year.  An equal amount on a 
matching basis will be contributed by the State Government/Urban Local Body (ULB).  As on 4 March 
2022, Government of India has released   ₹ 2,115 crore for Smart Cities in Gujarat, out of which ₹ 
1,887.86 crore (89%) has been utilized by these Smart Cities.  So far, Smart Cities in Gujarat have 
tendered out 344 projects worth ₹ 16,616.57 crore; work orders have been issued in 113 projects worth 
₹ 8,849.41 crore; 212 projects worth ₹ 5,688.17 crore have been completed. 
 
(c):  The period of implementation of SCM has been extended upto June 2023 and all Smart Cities 
are expected to complete their projects within the stipulated time.

TO BE ANSWERED ON MARCH 28, 2022 
 
ALLOCATION OF FUNDS IN SCM 
NO. 2796.   SHRI ABIR RANJAN BISWAS : 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
(a)  the cities under the Smart Cities Mission (SCM) and the details of funds allocated, 
released and utilised by them since the inception of the scheme, city-wise and year-wise; 
(b)  whether any funds have been spent to take low hanging electrical wires and other utility 
wires under the ground in any city which is under the Smart Cities Mission; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof, city-wise; and 
(d) the activities which have been undertaken for women's safety and the funds utilized for 
the same under the Smart Cities Mission, city-wise? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI KAUSHAL KISHORE) 
 
(a):  Government of India launched the Smart Cities Mission (SCM) on 25 June 2015. 100 Smart cities 
have been selected through 4 rounds of competition from January 2016 to June 2018. The list of 100 
Smart Cities selected in various rounds of Challenge under SCM is given in Annexure-I. As per SCM 
Guidelines, Central Government will provide financial support to the extent of ₹ 48,000 crore over five 
years i.e., on an average ₹ 100 crore per city per year.  An equal amount on a matching basis will be 
contributed by the State Government/Urban Local Body (ULB).  As on 4 March 2022, Government of 
India has released   ₹ 29,213.60 crore for 100 Smart Cities, out of which ₹ 25,177.65 crore (86%) has 
been utilized. The State/City-wise details of funds released by Central Government & utilization thereof 
by Smart Cities is given in Annexure-II. 
 
(b) & (c): Government of India through various programmatic interventions, assists States/UTs, both 
technically and financially, in their efforts towards urban development. SCM have taken several steps to 
address issues related to hazard risk caused by exposed wires and constant digging of multiple trenches in 
urban areas. These Cities are implementing around 780 Smart Road projects worth more than ₹ 26,700 
crore which, inter alia, include provisions of replacement of overhead wires with underground wiring, 
creation of utility ducts for common infrastructure to avoid multiple trenching etc.  
(d):  Integrated Command and Control Centers (ICCCs) have been operationalized in 76 Smart Cities 
in the country. These ICCCs are playing important role in ensuring better monitoring and efficiency in 
areas like traffic management, crowd management, detection of crimes etc.  Surveillance cameras, 
installed at strategic locations in various cities, help in ensuring safety of all residents of the area, 
including women. Projects such as smart streetlighting, traffic management, deployment of emergency 
call boxes, mobile apps are also contributing towards enhanced safety for women.

ESTABLISHMENT OF REAL ESTATE TRIBUNALS 
NO. 2797.  SMT. PRIYANKA CHATURVEDI : 
 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether all States have established Real Estate Tribunals; 
(b) the number of Real Estate Regulatory Authorities, State-wise details thereof; 
(c) the number of cases pending in Real Estate Tribunals; 
(d) the State-wise distributions of the number of pending cases in the Tribunals; 
(e) the average number of days taken to resolve pending cases; and 
(f) whether Government has taken any revised measures to protect the exploitation of homebuyers? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI KAUSHAL KISHORE) 
 
(a) to (e): As per the latest information available with the Ministry, 28 States/ Union Territories (UTs) 
have set up Real Estate Appellate Tribunal and 30 States/UTs have set up the Real Estate 
Regulatory Authority under Real Estate (Regulation & Development) Act, 2016 (RERA). 
State-wise implementation details are annexed . Information regarding number of cases 
pending and average time taken to resolve them in Real Estate Tribunals is not maintained 
centrally.  
  
(f): Various measures have been taken by the Government to protect the interest of homebuyers 
from time to time. RERA ensures to protect the interest of homebuyers by regulating and 
promoting in Real Estate Sector in a transparent and accountable manner. Section 4 of 
RERA provides for compulsory deposit of seventy percent of amount realised for real estate 
project from allottees in a separate bank account to cover the cost of construction and land 
cost. RERA also, interalia, makes the promoter liable for refund of amount, with interest and 
compensation, in case developer fails to complete or is unable to give possession of 
apartment, plot, building to homebuyer; as per the terms of the agreement for sale. 
 
 Moreover, in order to provide last mile funding to stalled real estate projects which are net-
worth positive and registered under RERA, a Special Window for Affordable and Mid 
Income Housing (SWAMIH) Investment Fund of Rs. 25,000 Crore has been created.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2799

SERVICES PROVIDED UNDER AMRUT 
 
NO. 2799.         SMT. GEETA ALIAS CHANDRAPRABHA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the services and facilities being provided under Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban 
Transformation Mission (AMRUT); and 
(b)  the action being taken to comply with the deadline for developing the cities covered under 
AMRUT, and the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI KAUSHAL KISHORE) 
 
(a): The Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) was launched on 25 
June 2015 in selected 500 cities and towns across all States and Union Territories (UTs). The Mission 
focuses on development of basic infrastructure in the selected cities in the sectors of water supply; 
sewerage and septage management; storm water drainage; green spaces and parks; and non-motorized 
urban transport.  Mission also executed a set of 11 reforms to improve governance of Urban Local 
Bodies (ULBs) and Capacity Building of ULBs.  
 
(b): Under AMRUT, against the total approved plan size of ₹77,640 crore, States/UTs have taken 
up 5,850 projects worth ₹81,283  crore. Of these, 4,158 projects worth ₹26,193 crore have been 
completed. So far, works worth ₹60,446 crore have been physically completed. 
 
Against the target to provide 139 lakh water tap connections to achieve universal water supply 
coverage and 145 lakh sewer connections to substantially enhance sewerage network coverage, 126 
lakh water tap connections and 95 lakh sewer connections (including septage management) have been 
provided under AMRUT and in convergence with other schemes. 
 
Implementation of AMRUT projects are periodically reviewed through video conferences, 
webinars and workshops etc. by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. There is a dedicated 
AMRUT web portal for tracking the implementation of AMRUT projects in the cities.  States/UTs 
are required to update data on the portal on regular basis. National Mission Directorate is also 
providing handholding support to the States/UTs and ULBs from time to time to resolve issues and 
eliminate bottlenecks for timely completion of projects.

water supply to every rural household of the country by 2024. 
At the time of announcement of Jal Jeevan Mission, out of 18.93 Crore rural households, 3.23 
Crore (17%) households were reported to have tap water connections. So far, 6.03 Crore 
(31.21%) rural households have been provided with tap water connections in last two and 
half years. Thus, as of date, out of 19.32 Crore rural households in the country, 9.26 Crore 
(47.97%) households are reported to have tap water supply in their homes. The State/ UT-
wise details are at Annex-I.

storm water drainage, non-motorized urban transport, and green spaces and parks. So far, out 
of target of providing 139 lakh tap connections to achieve universal water supply coverage in 
the selected cities, 126 lakh household water tap connections have been provided under 
AMRUT and in convergence with other schemes. State-wise details of household tap

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2801

WATER-SCARCE VILLAGES/CITIES 
 
2801. SHRI MD. NADIMUL HAQUE 
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI  be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government has conducted any recent studies to enumerate the number of cities and villages 
that will exhaust their water resources in the near future; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether Government has adopted any measures to address this issue; 
(d) if so, the details thereof, including coverage, budget allocation and status of implementation; and 
(e) whether Government is aware that a recent NITI Aayog report has predicted that by 2030 the demand 
for water supply will be twice the available supply? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
 
(SHRI BISHWESWAR TUDU) 
 
(a) & (b) Generally, water resource availability is assessed basin-wise.  As per the study titled 
“Reassessment of Water Availability in India using Space Inputs, 2019” conducted by Central Water 
Commission (CWC) in collaboration with National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), the average annual 
water resources availability in the country is assessed at 1,999.20 billion cubic metres (BCM). It is 
estimated that owing to topographic, hydrological and other constraints, the utilizable water is 1,126 BCM 
which comprises 690 BCM of surface water and 436 BCM of replenishable ground water. The water 
requirement of the country for high demand scenario for the year 2050 as per the National Commission on 
Integrated Water Resources Development (NCIWRD) Report-1999, is 1,180 BCM.
 
As per 2020 assessment by Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), out of 6,965 assessment units (Block/ 
Taluks/ Mandals/ watersheds/ Firkas) in the country, 1,114 units in 15 States/ UTs have been categorised as 
‘over-exploited’ where the Annual Ground Water Extraction is more than Annual Extractable Ground Water 
Resources. Further, as per the information available with CGWB, no city or village will exhaust its water 
resources in the near future.
 
(c) & (d) Water being a State subject, steps for augmentation, conservation and efficient management of 
water resources are primarily undertaken by the respective State Governments. In order to supplement the 
efforts of the State Governments, Central Government provides technical and financial assistance to them 
through various schemes and programmes.
 
  
The Government of India formulated a National Perspective Plan (NPP) of interlinking of rivers for 
transferring water from surplus basins to deficit basins/areas in 1980. National Water Development Agency 
(NWDA) has identified 30 links (16 under Peninsular Component and 14 under Himalayan Component) for 
preparation of Feasibility Reports/ Detailed Project Reports under Inter-linking of Rivers Project. However, 
river interlinking projects are largely dependent on consensus on water sharing between participating States.
 
  
Government of India, in partnership with States, is implementing Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) to make 
provision of potable tap water supply to every rural household of the country at the service level of 55 litre 
266

per capita per day by 2024. For ensuring tap water supply in drought-prone and water-scarce areas with 
inadequate rainfall or dependable ground water sources, provisions have been made under JJM for bulk 
water transfer from long distances and regional water supply schemes. In addition, provisions have been 
made for source recharging, viz. dedicated bore well recharge structures, rain water recharge, rejuvenation 
of existing water bodies, etc., in convergence with other schemes such as MGNREGS, Integrated Watershed 
Management Programme (IWMP), 15th Finance Commission tied grants to RLBs/ PRIs, State schemes, 
CSR funds, etc.
 
Government of India has launched AMRUT 2.0 on 1st October, 2021 for a period of 5 years (FY 2021- 22 
to 2025-26), with the objective of providing universal coverage of water supply through functional 
household tap connections in all statutory towns in the country. AMRUT 2.0 focuses on making specified 
cities water secure through recycle/reuse of treated sewage, rejuvenation of water bodies and water 
conservation. 
 
  
Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) was launched during the year 2015-16, with an aim to 
enhance physical access of water on farm and for expanding cultivable area under assured irrigation, 
improve on-farm water use efficiency, introducing sustainable water conservation practices, etc. During 
2016-17, ninety-nine (99) on-going major/medium irrigation projects in the country having balance 
estimated cost of Rs.77,595 crore under PMKSY-Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP) have 
been prioritised, in consultation with States, for completion in phases. The Command Area Development & 
Water Management (CADWM) Programme has been brought under Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee 
Yojana (PMKSY) – Har Khet Ko Pani from 2015-16 onwards. Implementation of PMKSY-AIBP and 
CAD&WM during 2021-26 has been approved by the Government of India with the central assistance of 
Rs. 23,918 crore. 
 
  
‘Sahi Fasal’ campaign was launched by National Water Mission (NWM) on 14.11.2019 to nudge farmers in 
the water stressed areas to grow crops which use water very efficiently, are economically remunerative, are 
healthy and nutritious, suited to the agro-climatic-hydro characteristics of the area, and are environment 
friendly.
 
Hon’ble Prime Minister launched the “Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain” (JSA:CTR) with the theme 
“Catch the Rain - Where it Falls When it Falls” on 22nd March 2021, the World Water Day, to cover all the 
districts  (rural as well as urban areas) across the country during 22nd March 2021 to 30th November 2021 - 
the pre-monsoon and monsoon period. JSA:CTR campaign had five focused interventions- (1) rainwater 
harvesting & water conservation; (2) enumerating, geo-tagging & making inventory of all water bodies, 
preparation of scientific plans for water conservation; (3) Setting up Jal Shakti Kendras in all districts; (4) 
intensive afforestation; and (5) awareness generation.
 
Government of India is also implementing Atal Bhujal Yojana, a central sector scheme with an outlay of 
Rs.6,000.00 crore. The scheme was launched by Hon'ble Prime Minister on 25.12.2019 and is being 
implemented in  seven States namely Haryana, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, 
Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. The focus of the scheme is on community participation and demand side 
intervention for sustainable ground water management in identified water stressed areas.  
 
  
Further, National Aquifer Mapping and Management program (NAQUIM) is being implemented by the 
Central Ground Water Board (CGWB)  facilitate sustainable management of groundwater resources in the 
country. 
 
  
(e) NITI Aayog in its report titled “Composite Water Management Index” published in June 2018, has 
referred to “McKinsey & WRG, ‘Charting our water future’, 2009” mentioning that by 2030, the country’s 
water demand is projected to be twice the available supply.  However, as mentioned in reply to parts (a) and 
(b) above, the utilizable water resource in the country is assessed at 1,126 BCM as against the projected 
water requirement in high demand scenario of 1,180 BCM in 2050.

2802    SHRI SUBHAS CHANDRA BOSE PILLI: 
            SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI: 
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government plans to have a sound financial management system in place to resolve 
the issue of non-timely release of States’ shares under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin); 
and 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof and, if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
 
                                                                      ANSWER 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI PRAHLAD SINGH  PATEL) 
 
(
a) & (b)  In the operational guidelines of Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) [SBM (G)] 
Phase-II, the States have been advised to release the Central share and proportionate State share 
funds from the State Treasury to the State level implementing agency, within 15 days from 
transfer of Central share to the State Governments.  Under the programme, in order to ensure 
timely release of States’ share, Central share funds are released only after release of 
proportionate State share against the previous instalment of Central share.  In this regard, a 
letter has also been written to the States on 14th May, 2020 stating that funds would not be 
released to the States without confirmation, inter alia, that proportionate State share has been 
released from the State Treasury against the previous instalment.  State Governments have also 
to confirm that necessary provision of State share has been made in the State’s Budget.  
Further, under SBM (G), all the States have also been on boarded on Public Financial 
Management System (PFMS) of Government of India so that effective monitoring of funds 
release (including State share) and its utilisation can be done.  The status of States’ share 
release is also included in every review meeting with the States.
